01 — Origin

How we
got here

SkyLakes started with a frustration we couldn't shake: India builds world-class small satellites, but there was nowhere to actually launch them on our own terms. Operators waited years for a ride-share slot, gave up control of their orbit, and still paid a premium.

So we started in a workshop with a simple bet — that a schedule-first vehicle built around proven solid propulsion could reach low Earth orbit for a fraction of the going rate. We machined our own motor, tested it, fired it, and wrote the flight software to fly it.

Today SkyLakes is a pre-seed company in Faridabad with a hardware-first team, a working Mission Control stack, and a launch roadmap aimed squarely at the gap no funded Indian player has filled: dedicated LEO access for under ₹40 crore.

02 — The Founders

Two people, one launch pad

Hardware and operations, sitting at the same bench since day one.

Aaditya Goswami

CEO & Cofounder

Aaditya leads propulsion, vehicle architecture, and the long game. He designed and fired SkyLakes' first in-house solid motor and owns the technical roadmap from SKYLX-S to -H. He spends most days between the test stand and the CAD screen, and the rest making the case to anyone who'll listen that India's launch cost curve can bend a lot faster than people think.

Ayush Seth

COO & Cofounder

Ayush runs operations, avionics, and everything that turns hardware into a company. He built the STM32 flight computer and the Mission Control dashboard, and he keeps the regulatory, funding, and customer tracks moving in parallel — iDEX, IN-SPACe, the LOI pipeline. If Aaditya makes it fly, Ayush makes sure there's a launch to fly it on.

03 — What we run on

Principles, not posters

01

Build it, then talk

We fire motors before we write pitch decks. Hardware in hand beats a roadmap every time.

02

Schedule is the product

A launch that slips isn't a launch. We pick proven propulsion precisely because it flies on time.

03

Cheap, on purpose

Under ₹40 crore to LEO isn't a discount — it's the whole design constraint we optimize against.
